questions.stem: A $5\ \text{kg}$ block rests on a rough horizontal floor with $\mu_s = 0.4$ and $\mu_k = 0.25$. A horizontal force of $15\ \text{N}$ is applied to it. Taking $g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, the friction force acting on the block is

options.whyWrong: $20\ \text{N}$ is the *maximum* static friction, not the actual value.
Kinetic friction applies only if the block slides, and it doesn't.
Friction is not zero. It must oppose the applied force to keep the block at rest.

questions.solution:
**Key idea:** check whether the block moves before choosing a friction formula.

1. Limiting static friction $= \mu_s mg = 0.4 \times 50 = 20\ \text{N}$
2. Applied force $15\ \text{N} < 20\ \text{N}$, so the block stays at rest.
3. Static friction balances the applied force: **$f = 15\ \text{N}$**
hints: Compare the applied force with $\mu_s N$.
If the block does not move, what must the net horizontal force be?
